On/Off Labels listing copy vs switch-label engineering — two different jobs

Teams assume On/Off Labels compatibility covers storefront language. iOS, UIAccessibility, and Connect actually separate in-app switch chrome from product-page copy:

  • On/Off Labels in the app — UIAccessibility.isOnOffSwitchLabelsEnabled checks, UISwitch adaptations when labels are on, custom toggle implementations that show I/O or 1/0 markers, and switch rows that remain readable when color alone cannot convey state. Engineering inside the binary — outside AppLocale scope.
  • Switch and toggle implementation — distinguishing custom toggles from system switches, ensuring on/off state is visible beyond green/gray color cues, and testing layouts when I/O labels appear beside controls. Engineering — not listing rewrite.
  • Switch-label marketing on the product page — description paragraphs, subtitle positioning, keywords, promotional text, and screenshot overlays that tell buyers your app respects On/Off Labels or offers clearer switch states. Connect text fields — this page.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China storefront. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, and screenshot caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of On/Off Labels support in the app.

An On/Off Labels-compatible app and a localized China listing are both valuable — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe switch-state clarity on the store page, not whether I/O labels render inside the app.

On/Off Labels vs Button Shapes, Bold Text, Increase Contrast, and Reduce Transparency — disambiguation

Apple groups several toggles under Settings → Accessibility → Display & Text Size. Indie teams conflate them on one product page. AppLocale covers On/Off Labels and switch-label marketing on listing metadata — not the other toggles:

  • On/Off Labels (this page) — I/O or 1/0 labels on switches and toggles so on/off state is readable without relying on color alone. Gallery frames may show Settings → Display & Text Size → On/Off Labels toggles, before/after switch-label comparisons, or "Respects On/Off Labels" badges. zh-Hans terms: 开关标签, 显示开关标签.
  • Button Shapes (different) — underlines, borders, and shape outlines on tappable buttons and links so controls stand apart from plain text. See Button Shapes listing guide — button-outline marketing is not switch-label copy.
  • Bold Text (different) — system-wide heavier font weight across the interface. See Bold Text listing guide — 粗体文本 heavier type is not 开关标签 switch labels.
  • Increase Contrast (different) — stronger contrast between foreground UI elements and backgrounds. See Increase Contrast listing guide — 增强对比度 UI contrast is not switch-label marketing.
  • Reduce Transparency (different) — reduces blur, vibrancy, and translucent backgrounds system-wide. See Reduce Transparency listing guide — 降低透明度 frosted-glass opacity is not toggle-label copy.
  • Larger Text (different) — adjustable font size via the text size slider. See Larger Text listing guide — 更大字体 typography scaling is not switch-label marketing.
  • Display Accommodations (different) — color filters, invert colors, smart invert, reduce white point, differentiate without color. See Display Accommodations listing guide — color and contrast presets, not switch-label overlays.
  • Dynamic Type (different) — scalable typography APIs and UIFontMetrics support. See Dynamic Type listing guide — not switch-label copy.
  • Reduce Motion (different) — toned-down animations and motion-sensitive accessibility. See Reduce Motion listing guide — not switch-label marketing.
  • Auto Brightness (different) — automatic display brightness under Display & Brightness — a separate path from Accessibility switch labels. Do not conflate 自动亮度 with 开关标签 on listing copy.

Your gallery may show an On/Off Labels toggle on one frame and a Button Shapes comparison on the next — but listing copy should name each claim accurately per frame. A switch-label demo is not a button-outline underline, not a Bold Text weight comparison, and not a color-filter picker unless that is what the screenshot shows.

What On/Off Labels actually does — listing honesty

Apple ships On/Off Labels in iOS and iPadOS Settings → Accessibility → Display & Text Size. When enabled, the system adds I/O or 1/0 labels on switches and toggles — making on/off state visible beyond green/gray or other color-only cues. Third-party apps may complement this with custom toggle styling when UIAccessibility.isOnOffSwitchLabelsEnabled is true. AppLocale rewrites listing copy from what your US page already claims:

  • If your app complements system On/Off Labels — zh-Hans copy can describe clearer switch states, visible I/O markers, or respects On/Off Labels workflows your binary actually ships — without claiming to replace the system setting unless your English listing already states that accurately.
  • If your app ships custom toggle UI — description and screenshot overlays should name the switch-state benefits you deliver (开关标签, 开关状态更清晰, 显示开关标签) in commerce-idiomatic Chinese, not generic "accessibility does everything" overclaims.
  • Separate On/Off Labels from Button Shapes in copy — Button Shapes adds outlines to tappable buttons and links; On/Off Labels adds I/O or 1/0 markers on switches. Listing vocabulary must follow your English lead feature and gallery frames.
  • Separate On/Off Labels from Differentiate Without Color — differentiate without color is a Display Accommodations preset for shape-based differentiation; On/Off Labels is a dedicated switch-label toggle. Do not conflate 不用颜色区分 with 开关标签 unless your English listing markets both accurately.
  • If your US page overclaims — AppLocale aligns zh-Hans strings to your English source; we do not invent broader On/Off Labels scope than your screenshots and description support.

Clear zh-Hans copy helps buyers who rely on switch labels understand your toggle-state story before install. It does not replace UIAccessibility checks in the binary, switch-label engineering, or Apple's review decisions.

On/Off Labels-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Switch-label marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe On/Off Labels — not a literal paste of US marketing:

On/Off Labels vs generic "clear toggles"

US pages use "Respects On/Off Labels", "Clearer switch states", or "I/O labels on toggles." China storefront copy often uses 显示开关标签, 开关标签, or 开关状态更清晰 — depending on whether you mean Apple's On/Off Labels setting specifically, custom in-app toggle styling, or general switch-state design. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual scope, not inventing On/Off Labels support your app does not ship.

On/Off Labels vs Button Shapes — do not conflate

On/Off Labels adds I/O or 1/0 markers on switches and toggles. Button Shapes adds underlines and borders to tappable buttons and links across the interface. zh-Hans listing copy should not imply 按钮形状 when your English source only markets switch labels. See the Button Shapes listing guide only if button-outline affordances are your lead marketing claim.

On/Off Labels vs Bold Text and Increase Contrast

Bold Text makes all system text heavier — 粗体文本. Increase Contrast intensifies foreground-background separation — 增强对比度. On/Off Labels adds visible markers on switch chrome — 开关标签. Each toggle has distinct buyer vocabulary and should not appear interchangeably in one keyword field unless your English listing genuinely markets all three.

On/Off Labels vs Reduce Transparency and Larger Text

Reduce Transparency removes blur and frosted effects — 降低透明度. Larger Text enlarges typography via the text size slider — 更大字体. On/Off Labels affects switch and toggle label chrome specifically. zh-Hans copy should not imply 降低透明度 or 更大字体 when your gallery only shows switch-label demos.

I/O vs 1/0 label phrasing

Apple's system labels may show "I" and "O" or "1" and "0" depending on locale and iOS version. zh-Hans listing copy can reference 开关标签 or 显示开关标签 for the setting name, and describe the benefit (开关状态不依赖颜色 alone) without over-specifying I/O vs 1/0 unless your English gallery shows one style consistently.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need switch-label search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 开关标签, 显示开关标签, and 开关状态 each signal different intent from Button Shapes or Increase Contrast keywords.

Caption lines vs burned-in badges

Marketing screenshot overlays you control — "Respects On/Off Labels" headlines on gallery frames showing Settings → Accessibility → Display & Text Size → On/Off Labels — are separate caption fields or burned-in PNG text. See Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese for caption-field mechanics when overlays are editable in Connect.

AppLocale FAQ

What is Apple On/Off Labels and why does listing copy matter?

On/Off Labels is under Settings → Accessibility → Display & Text Size → On/Off Labels. When enabled, iOS adds I/O or 1/0 labels on switches and toggles so on/off state is readable without relying on color alone. Marketing that feature on your en-US page does not auto-fill zh-Hans Connect fields.

Does shipping On/Off Labels support auto-translate my China listing?

No. On/Off Labels compatibility is in-app UI engineering — it does not create or fill a Simplified Chinese localization row. Empty or English zh-Hans fields mean China buyers see en-US fallback on the product page.

What listing fields does AppLocale rewrite for On/Off Labels apps?

Paste-ready Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans) copy for App Store Connect listing fields you specify: title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot overlay or caption lines that mention On/Off Labels, switch state labels, or I/O labels — rewritten from your English originals with terms like 开关标签 and 显示开关标签 where accurate.

How is this different from Button Shapes, Bold Text, or Increase Contrast?

On/Off Labels listing copy markets I/O or 1/0 labels on switches and toggles. Button Shapes covers underlines on tappable buttons. Bold Text covers heavier system-wide text weight. Increase Contrast covers stronger UI contrast. Each is a separate Display & Text Size toggle — do not reuse boilerplate across them.

How is this different from Display Accommodations or Differentiate Without Color?

Display Accommodations covers color filters, invert colors, and reduce white point. Differentiate Without Color is a Display Accommodations preset. On/Off Labels covers switch and toggle label chrome — different buyer intent and screenshot vocabulary.

Does AppLocale implement On/Off Labels in my app?

No. We deliver listing metadata copy only. UIAccessibility.isOnOffSwitchLabelsEnabled checks, UISwitch label styling, and in-app UI work are outside AppLocale scope. We rewrite how you describe existing switch-label features on the store page — we do not implement them in the app.

What character limits apply to zh-Hans On/Off Labels fields?

App name and subtitle are each up to 30 characters. Keywords allow up to 100 characters. Description and screenshot caption lines have longer limits but should stay concise — especially overlays that must fit on-device mockups.
